content:
alex: quick sync — proposal for deprecating /v1/generate. thinking of 3 things: a soft gate (client opt-in cohorts), a route-level feature switch, and a short rollforward window for emergency fixes. thoughts?
maya: sounds reasonable. can you sketch how cohorts picked? random? by tenant size?
alex: initial cohort = 1% random + all internal tenants. then ramp by usage and error rate. we gate by an HTTP header: `X-Feature-Gate: v2-gate-<cohort>` so we can route in infra.
sam: re: header, watch caching layers. edge CDNs might strip unknown headers. need header pass-through test.
ria: also think about SDKs — we'll add an opt-in flag in client SDKs so apps can signal opt-in without header fiddling. devex-bot: note: add SDK flag needs minor semver bump, doc update.
maya: question: how do we measure rollout safety? metrics + regression tests?
alex: plan: realtime metrics for latency, error-rate, generation-quality (via eval hooks). threshold: if latency increases >10% or error-rate >0.5% over baseline, auto-rollback the cohort.
sam: auto-rollback is scope creep in routing infra. is it possible to do automated rollback or should we send alerts and manual ops roll?
alex: prefer automated for the first 1% and canary. full rollouts manual. infra-bot: FYI: we can add a circuit-breaker that drops to v1 variant if anomalies fire. requires QA + short runbook.
ria: we need to decide shim cost. Keeping a compatibility shim in the runtime for 6 months vs. removing earlier — impacts memory and perf. what's the business tolerance?
maya: product prefers 6 months public notice. but from infra side, if shim adds <5% p95 latency we can tolerate longer.
sam: to quantify: add microbench job that runs both paths and reports p95 overhead weekly. add to eng-ml CI.
alex: agree. also propose a formal deprecation header we serve in responses: `Deprecation: v1; sunset=2026-10-01` for all clients hitting old route. devex-bot: we'll draft docs + email template.
ria: rollout telemetry: collect by tenant, by SDK version, and by route. export to a dashboard (console -> deprecations view).
maya: on migrations: provide a compatibility shim that maps old `instructions` key to `messages` shape for 3 months, with a warning in logs. after 3 months we turn off mapping for non-opted-in cohorts.
sam: testing: need forward-compat tests: v2 client against v1 runtime and vice versa. add to canary harness.
alex: one more thing: migration escape hatch — on error spike, route all traffic to a low-cost fallback model (smaller model) rather than full rollback, to preserve availability. should we allow that?
maya: yes, fallback model OK, but must be transparent to customers. cost impact estimate needed.
ria: summary action items: 1) infra: header pass-through test + circuit-breaker wiring (sam). 2) devex: SDK opt-in flag + docs (ria). 3) eng-ml: perf microbench + compat tests (sam, maya). 4) product: draft deprecation timeline (alex). 5) observability: dashboard for deprecations and auto-alerts (maya).
alex: I'll write an RFC fragment and a short runbook for rollback/escape hatch. ping me if you want to be added to reviewers.
maya: ok, will slot quick design review tomorrow 10:30am.
sam: noted. I'll start the pass-through test and CI job.
infra-bot: deploy-check: header-pass test added to staging.
devex-bot: docs-draft created: /docs/migrations/v1-to-v2-draft.md
alex: thanks all — neat and small; aim to keep initial rollout conservative. :thumbsup:
